newsitem.title: USA: National Steel furnace output normalizes.
newsitem.headline: National Steel furnace output normalizes.

text.p: National Steel Corp said Wednesday that blast furnace production is back to normal after unplanned outages at both furnaces in its Granite City division that hurt third-quarter operating results.
The steelmaker reported net income of $24.3 million, or $0.50 per share, on the quarter, compared with net income of $21.0 million, or $0.42 per share, a year ago.

Quarterly results were helped by a gain of $3.7 million from sale of property, adjustments to employee benefit related liabilities and settlement of a dispute with the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp on a joint venture's benefit plan.
These nonrecurring gains totaled about $13 million, net of tax. Excluding these items, third quarter net income totaled $11.2 million, or $0.20 per share.
Sales for the quarter rose to $736 million as compared with $725 million in the third quarter of 1995.

"We were able to offset much of the production decline (caused by the furnace outages) such that shipments still exceeded last year's third quarter level. Blast furnace production is back to normal levels, and we expect our shipments to respond accordingly," National Steel chairman and chief executive Osamu Sawaragi.
